title: I got fired twice. It led me to start my own company.
excerpt: Alex Stephany says getting fired twice pushed him toward entrepreneurship. He now leads Beam, an AI startup with about 200 employees.
content_html:
I got fired twice before I turned 30. It was the best thing that happened in my career.

As told to Kelly Burch

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

This as-told-to essay is based on a conversation with Alex Stephany, founder of Beam. It has been edited for length and clarity.

I was always a good student, but when I graduated from Oxford and entered the workforce, I immediately felt like a fish out of water.

One of my first weekends working as a lawyer, I went on a corporate retreat. I remember feeling that everyone else in the room was much better suited to the work of being a lawyer than I was.

Two years later, when my contract was up, I wasn't surprised that my employer didn't renew it. I tried my hand at management consulting, but even in a different job, I felt ill at ease in the corporate world. I was fired from the consulting role after about four years.

That was quite scary. I had been really successful in life as a student, but I worried I was ill-suited to adulting. At Oxford, everyone became a doctor, lawyer, banker, or consultant — if I couldn't succeed in those careers, I worried I wouldn't succeed at all.

A smartphone unlocked new career options for me

I was lucky that I could go home and live with my parents. I didn't have children to support. Even so, I had some really dark moments in the months after I was fired. I just didn't know what to do with my life. Being fired not once, but twice, felt like proof that I was bad at adulting.

It became worse as I entered my 30s. I was doing some writing work, but I was embarrassed to be underemployed at this stage of life. When friends wanted to catch up, I worried about being the object of their pity.

During that time, I wasn't spending much money. Because of that, I got a smartphone late. Once I had it in my hands, however, I saw it was going to transform everything. I started going to tech events and applying to startups. I would walk into rooms feeling shy and embarrassed, but force myself to ask people for coffee. That's when my life started to change.

I became CEO, then founded my own company

I don't want to downplay how traumatic and upsetting being fired was. But looking back, I can see how being fired was a catalyst for my career. Now, when I'm asked about the people who helped me, I name those bosses who fired me from roles I wasn't good at.

I got hired in the startup space and eventually became the CEO of JustPark, an app that connects Londoners with parking. In 2017, I founded Beam, which uses AI to better empower social service workers. We have about 200 employees worldwide, and the technology is used in five countries.

Years of being underemployed forced me to build resilience and adaptability that have served me well as a CEO. People who have only been successful in life aren't suited to work in a startup, because you're constantly failing when you try to get something off the ground.

I've found success in social entrepreneurship

Today, I know that I'm not fundamentally bad at being an adult. I'm just not wired for a corporate, institutional role. That makes sense, because I've always been a bit of a rebel. Entrepreneurship is a much better role for me.

While the average tech CEO might strive to be like Elon Musk, billionaires aren't my role models. My family always taught me that successful people are those who help others, and that's who I grew up admiring. My great-grandfather was a businessman who helped Jews resettle in London before World War II. He was a social entrepreneur before that, as a term — and I'm proud to follow in his footsteps.

content_html_zh:
在我30岁之前，我被解雇了两次。 这是我职业生涯中发生的最好的事情。

正如凯莉·伯奇 (Kelly Burch) 所说，您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

这篇文章基于与 Beam 创始人 Alex Stephany 的对话。 为了篇幅和清晰度，对其进行了编辑。

我一直是一个好学生，但当我从牛津大学毕业并进入职场时，我立刻感觉就像一条离开水的鱼。

在我作为律师工作的第一个周末，我参加了一次公司静修活动。 我记得我感觉房间里的其他人都比我更适合律师的工作。

两年后，当我的合同到期时，我的雇主没有续签我并不感到惊讶。 我尝试过管理咨询，但即使从事不同的工作，我在企业界也感到不自在。 大约四年后，我被解雇了。

那是相当可怕的。 作为一名学生，我的生活非常成功，但我担心自己不适合成人。 在牛津，每个人都成为了医生、律师、银行家或顾问——如果我不能在这些职业中取得成功，我担心我根本不会成功。

智能手机为我开启了新的职业选择

我很幸运，我可以回家和父母住在一起。 我没有孩子需要抚养。 即便如此，在我被解雇后的几个月里，我还是经历了一些非常黑暗的时刻。 我只是不知道我的人生该怎么办。 被解雇不是一次，而是两次，感觉就像是我不善于成熟的证据。

当我进入30多岁时，情况变得更糟。 我当时正在做一些写作工作，但我对在人生的这个阶段没有充分就业感到尴尬。 当朋友们想要追赶时，我担心成为他们怜悯的对象。

那段时间我并没有花多少钱。 正因为如此，我才迟到了智能手机。 然而，一旦我把它拿到手，我就看到它会改变一切。 我开始参加科技活动并申请初创公司。 我走进房间时会感到害羞和尴尬，但强迫自己向人们要咖啡。 从那时起我的生活开始改变。

我成为首席执行官，然后创办了自己的公司

我不想淡化被解雇是多么痛苦和令人沮丧。 但回想起来，我可以看到被解雇是如何成为我职业生涯的催化剂的。 现在，当我被问及帮助过我的人时，我会说出那些将我从我不擅长的职位上解雇的老板的名字。

我在初创公司被录用，并最终成为 JustPark 的首席执行官，JustPark 是一款将伦敦人与停车联系起来的应用程序。 2017年，我创立了Beam，利用人工智能更好地赋能社会服务工作者。 我们在全球拥有约 200 名员工，该技术在五个国家使用。

多年的就业不足迫使我培养韧性和适应能力，这对我担任首席执行官很有帮助。 那些在生活中取得成功的人不适合在初创公司工作，因为当你试图取得进展时，你会不断失败。

我在社会创业方面取得了成功

今天，我知道我作为一个成年人从根本上来说并不差。 我只是不适合担任公司、机构的角色。 这是有道理的，因为我一直有点叛逆。 创业对我来说是一个更好的角色。

虽然普通科技公司首席执行官可能会努力成为埃隆·马斯克(Elon Musk)，但亿万富翁并不是我的榜样。 我的家人总是告诉我，成功的人是那些帮助别人的人，这就是我从小到大崇拜的人。 我的曾祖父是一位商人，他在二战前帮助犹太人在伦敦重新定居。 在此之前，他是一名社会企业家，我很自豪能追随他的脚步。
